growing_specifications.description: High-value temperate brassica crop cultivated in Cordillera highlands (Benguet, Mountain Province) and Bukidnon plateau, as well as lowland cool dry season. Produces compact, layered heads of crisp leaves.

category_why.title: Why is Cabbage classified under Leafy / Brassica?
category_why.summary: Cabbage is a head-forming cruciferous leafy vegetable belonging to the Brassicaceae (mustard) family alongside pechay, broccoli, and cauliflower.
points: Cruciferous Family Morphology: Possesses cross-shaped flowers and produces overlapping waxy rosette leaves rich in glucosinolates and sulfur compounds.
Head-Forming Rosette: Central leaves fold tightly inward to form a compact spherical or flat-round head protecting the tender inner growing point.
Clubroot Susceptibility: Shares genetic vulnerability to Plasmodiophora brassicae (Clubroot), strictly requiring 2–3 year crop rotation away from brassicas.

harvest_why.title: Why is the harvest maturity set to 70–90 days?
harvest_why.summary: Captures dense, rock-solid heads at full weight (1.5–3 kg) before outer leaves crack or internal stem bolting occurs.
points: Nursery Germination & Plugs (Days 1–30): Seeds germinate in 4–7 days; seedlings develop 4–5 sturdy true leaves in plug trays before transplanting.
Vegetative Rosette Expansion (Days 31–50): Broad outer leaves expand outward collecting maximum sunlight for energy storage.
Head Initiation & Filling (Days 51–75): Center leaves curl inward forming a tight ball; requires high moisture and potassium (potash).
Firm Head Harvest Window (Days 75–90): Heads feel completely solid and firm to thumb pressure; cut in early morning leaving 2–3 protective wrapper leaves.

watering_why.title: Why does Cabbage require consistent watering every 2–3 days?
watering_why.summary: Consistent root-zone moisture is required for rapid cell expansion in overlapping head leaves and to prevent head splitting and tip-burn.
points: High Transpiration & Water Volume: 92% of the cabbage head is water; uneven drought cycles cause bitter, fibrous leaves and small loose heads.
Head Splitting Prevention: Sudden heavy rain after prolonged dry spells causes explosive internal leaf growth that ruptures the outer head.
Calcium Tip-Burn Defense: Calcium moves only through xylem water flow; erratic watering starves inner leaf margins, turning them brown and necrotic.

soil_why.title: Why does Cabbage require well-drained loam with pH 6.0–6.8?
soil_why.summary: Slightly acidic to neutral fertile soil prevents Clubroot infection while providing balanced macronutrient uptake.
points: Clubroot Suppression: Soil pH below 5.5 triggers rapid germination of dormant Plasmodiophora resting spores; applying agricultural lime keeps pH safely above 6.5.
Heavy Nutrient Mining: Deep, rich organic loam supplies substantial nitrogen for leafy canopy and potassium for dense head packing.

varieties.description: Leading heat-tolerant flat-headed cabbage hybrid in the Philippines. Produces dense 1.5–2.5 kg heads with excellent shipping endurance and mild sweet flavor.
Premier highland hybrid with strong tolerance to tip-burn and bolting, producing heavy spherical dark-green heads.
